Paper: Is ChatGPT Good at Search? Investigating Large Language Models as Re-Ranking Agents
Mechanism: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 given a query plus a fixed candidate list already produced by a first-stage retriever (BM25/dense retrieval); the LLM outputs a reordered permutation of that list. It never generates or selects candidates outside the supplied set.
DecisionAuthority: Hybrid -- LLM output is the ranking used by the downstream IR system directly (not human-gated); no deferral to a human built into the method itself
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- matches the 'reranks already-retrieved candidates only, never classifies from blank input' half of the constraint exactly, and is the direct methodological ancestor of ADS-Cascade's T3 mechanism. Does NOT match the 'output never auto-applied, always routed to human' half -- RankGPT's output is auto-applied as the final ranking.
KeyNotes: Founding paper (RankGPT) of a very large sub-literature (dozens of direct descendants) establishing LLM-constrained-to-reranking as thoroughly standard IR practice. 590 citations.
VerificationMethod: DOI resolved via FastTrack/OpenAlex, cross-confirmed by Consensus (citation count) and independent search.

Paper: Zero-Shot Listwise Document Reranking with a Large Language Model
Mechanism: 'LRL': LLM given a fixed candidate document set from a first-stage retriever and generates a reordered list of document IDs; explicitly contrasted with pointwise methods that also require a pre-existing candidate pool.
DecisionAuthority: LLM/system has final authority (ranking used directly); no human gate
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- candidates-only constraint present; no-auto-apply/human-review constraint absent.
KeyNotes: Reinforces that 'LLM sees only pre-filtered candidates' is baseline design in this literature, not a novel restriction.

Paper: Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting
Mechanism: LLM compares pairs of already-retrieved candidates to produce a ranking; strictly reranking over a supplied set.
KeyNotes: One of dozens of 'LLM listwise/pairwise reranker' variants (RankZephyr, RankVicuna, FIRST, ListT5, PE-Rank, REARANK, etc.) -- the mechanism itself is commodity technique by 2023-2025.

Paper: Fine-Tuning LLaMA for Multi-Stage Text Retrieval
Mechanism: RepLLaMA (retriever) + RankLLaMA (pointwise reranker), the latter scoring only candidates passed from the retrieval stage.
KeyNotes: Confirms the 'retrieve-then-LLM-rerank' pipeline is the dominant IR paradigm, not an ADS-Cascade innovation.

Paper: Architecting Human-AI Systems for Effective Collaboration and Oversight: Making Sense of Human/AI-in/on/Over/Under/Along-the-Loop
Mechanism: Formal taxonomy distinguishing 'human approver' architectures (system presents a planned action; cannot act without approval) from 'human selector' architectures (human picks from a filtered/narrowed list of possible actions -- explicitly likened to route suggestions).
DecisionAuthority: Human has final authority (by construction of the category)
Domain: General -- synthesizes human-machine/human-computer/human-robot interaction literature across domains
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- closest single terminological match found for the 'human must confirm, AI proposes/filters' half of the constraint. Their 'human selector from a filtered list' is structurally identical to ADS-Cascade routing filtered/reranked candidates to a human. Does not discuss LLMs, reranking, or a deterministic-cascade context, and does not combine this with the 'never given blank-slate classification' restriction.
KeyNotes: 2025 taxonomy explicitly built to clean up inconsistent 'human-in/on/over-the-loop' terminology -- its existence and stated motivation is itself evidence the field lacks one settled name for ADS-Cascade's exact configuration.
VerificationMethod: get_paper DOI lookup confirmed via OpenAlex; abstract and taxonomy text retrieved via Scholar Gateway full-text passages.

Paper: Human at the Center: A Framework for Human-Driven AI Development
Authors: Hu, Navas, Gaube, Mozannar, Taylor, Dvijotham, Bondi-Kelly
Mechanism: Defines four human-AI design modes; Mode 1 'AI Supports Human Decisions': AI generates predictions/recommendations/insights to aid human decision making, but the human is accountable for the final decision -- AI always defers final judgment to humans. Mode 2 'AI Decides Unless Uncertain' separately covers confidence-triggered deferral/abstention.
DecisionAuthority: Human has final authority (in Mode 1, by definition)
Domain: General human-AI system design (healthcare, hiring, criminal justice examples cited)
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- a named, citable formalization of 'AI recommends, human decides, always,' precisely ADS-Cascade's stated authority split, but as a general design mode, not tied to LLM reranking-of-candidates or a deterministic-cascade architecture.
KeyNotes: Co-authored by Hussein Mozannar, a lead author of the learning-to-defer literature (see G2-08) -- this paper is where the L2D and decision-support literatures converge on shared terminology.
VerificationMethod: Full text retrieved via Scholar Gateway; OpenAlex venue/DOI cross-checked.

Paper: Algorithmic Decision-Making Safeguarded by Human Knowledge
Mechanism: Proposes a 'guardrail/clipping' model where a human analyst can only cap or floor an algorithmic output if it appears unreasonable -- a restricted, bounded form of human override, explicitly contrasted against the learning-to-defer literature where a full decision is substituted.
ConstraintType: Other (bounded-override, distinct from both pure recommendation and full deferral)
DecisionAuthority: Hybrid (algorithm decides by default; human intervention structurally limited to clipping, not full override)
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Distinct -- mechanism (numeric clipping) is not the same shape as ADS-Cascade's candidate-reranking-plus-human-review.
KeyNotes: Valuable primarily as a 2026 literature map confirming 'learning to defer' is the standard academic home for this general problem class (cites Madras et al. 2018, Mozannar and Sontag 2020, Bansal et al. 2019/2021, Wilder et al. 2021, Keswani et al. 2021, Donahue et al. 2022, Rastogi et al. 2022, Raghu et al. 2019).
VerificationMethod: get_paper DOI lookup confirmed via OpenAlex.

Paper: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
Mechanism: Model jointly learns a classifier and a 'rejector' deciding, per instance, whether the model predicts or defers to a human expert -- direct methodological successor to Madras, Pitassi and Zemel's original learning-to-defer formulation.
ConstraintType: Deferral-to-deterministic-mechanism (the rejector is the deterministic gate)
DecisionAuthority: Hybrid -- model decides confidently, human decides otherwise
Domain: General classification (child welfare screening, radiology in follow-on work)
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- canonical academic name for 'confidence/determinism gates whether a model or a human handles the case,' structurally the same idea underlying ADS-Cascade's tier-routing logic, though L2D papers train a joint deferral policy rather than using a pre-set determinism metric, and L2D's 'defer' branch hands the full task to a human rather than a reranked candidate list.
KeyNotes: Also catalogued as B5-02 in the main literature matrix; spawned a large sub-field (Keswani et al. 2021, Hemmer et al. 2023, Alves et al. 2025 OpenL2D/FiFAR, Lykouris and Weng 2024) -- the standard term of art a reviewer would expect ADS-Cascade positioned against.

Paper: Trustworthy and Practical AI for Healthcare: A Guided Deferral System with Large Language Models
Mechanism: An LLM parses medical reports for disorder classification and, using a 'guided deferral' mechanism, defers uncertain predictions to humans with intelligent guidance rather than a blank accept/reject.
DecisionAuthority: Hybrid (LLM decides confidently, defers uncertain cases to human)
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- closest single paper found that combines 'LLM' + 'classification task' + 'confidence-triggered deferral to human.' Does not involve reranking of pre-retrieved candidates (its LLM classifies directly rather than reordering a rules-layer's shortlist), so the 'never given blank-slate classification' leg of ADS-Cascade's constraint is absent here.
KeyNotes: Strongest single LLM-specific analog found for the deferral half, but architecturally simpler than ADS-Cascade (no upstream retrieval/candidate-generation layer constraining the LLM's input).
VerificationMethod: OpenAlex/FastTrack record (DOI and venue present); duplicate arXiv preprint independently found.

Paper: Learning to Defer in Congested Systems: The AI-Human Interplay
Mechanism: Models content moderation as an AI-human pipeline: AI makes classification and admission (send-to-human) decisions; humans review admitted items and can overturn erroneous AI classifications; reviews are also training data.
ConstraintType: Deferral-to-deterministic-mechanism (admission thresholding) + requires-human-confirmation for admitted items
DecisionAuthority: Hybrid -- AI auto-decides low-risk items, human has final say on admitted (uncertain/high-risk) items
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous -- closely mirrors ADS-Cascade's tiered structure (deterministic layer routes by confidence; uncertain cases get human review), but the AI here is a risk classifier making a direct decision, not an LLM constrained to reranking pre-fetched candidates, and the AI is explicitly permitted to auto-delete content without human review at high confidence -- unlike ADS-Cascade's 'always routes to human review' invariant for its LLM tier.
KeyNotes: Strong structural analog for the cascade-with-confidence-routing shape, weak analog for the specific 'never auto-applied' invariant.

Paper: Towards Unbiased and Accurate Deferral to Multiple Experts
Mechanism: Classifier + deferral system that routes low-confidence cases to one or more human experts; tested on a content-moderation dataset.
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous (same L2D family as G2-08; not LLM- or reranking-specific).
KeyNotes: Also catalogued as B5-04 in the main literature matrix.

Paper: Human-AI Collaboration via Conditional Delegation: A Case Study of Content Moderation
Mechanism: Proposes 'conditional delegation' -- humans author rules specifying which regions of the model's output space are trustworthy enough for the AI to act on unsupervised, versus regions still requiring human review.
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous to the route-to-human-when-uncertain logic; distinct on the LLM/reranking specifics.
KeyNotes: One of the few papers explicitly framing 'which cases the AI may decide alone vs. must be routed to a human' as a first-class design variable -- close to ADS-Cascade's per-item determinism gating, though ADS-Cascade sends 100% of its LLM tier to human review rather than conditionally.

Paper: Liable, but Not in Control? Ensuring Meaningful Human Agency in Automated Decision-Making Systems
Mechanism: Coins 'quasi-automation' for systems where a human is nominally in the loop as a 'rubber-stamping mechanism' over an otherwise fully automated decision; proposes criteria to distinguish genuine ('meaningful') human agency from token sign-off, examined for self-driving cars, border searches, and content moderation.
ConstraintType: Requires-human-confirmation (critiqued as often not meaningful in practice)
DecisionAuthority: Human has final authority nominally -- the paper's whole point is this can be illusory
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Analogous framing tool -- directly useful for a reviewer asking whether ADS-Cascade's human-review step is meaningful or rubber-stamping. Not a description of an LLM-reranker system.
KeyNotes: Establishes that regulatory/legal scholarship has produced explicit criteria for genuine vs. cosmetic human final authority, relevant to how rigorously ADS-Cascade should defend its 'always routes to human' claim.

Paper: Automated decision-making in the EU Member States: The right to explanation and other 'suitable safeguards' in the national legislations
Mechanism: Surveys GDPR Art. 22(3) safeguards, including the statutory 'right to obtain human intervention,' across EU member-state implementations.
ConstraintType: Requires-human-confirmation (as a legal mandate, not a system design choice)
EquivalenceToADSCascadeConstraint: Distinct -- this is the regulatory driver/rationale for 'keep a human in the loop,' not a technical description of how an LLM would be architecturally constrained to comply. Confirms GDPR Art. 22 has generated academic literature, but it is legal/policy analysis, not a systems paper describing an LLM-reranker pattern.
KeyNotes: Confirms the mission's hypothesis that a regulatory literature exists, but it doesn't describe ADS-Cascade's specific mechanism.
